events.content:
I now have a clear picture of the setup. Let me explain what I found and the precise change needed. ## Current behavior The project route (`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`) wraps a single async `` component in one ``. That component awaits both `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` together via `Promise.all`. Because `getProjectDetails` has an artificial 800ms delay, the whole subtree — including the `

{title}

` — stays behind the `Loading project...` fallback until both resolve. On the dashboard (`app/page.tsx`), the links are plain `` with no prefetching control. With `cacheComponents: true` enabled, Next.js would prefetch the full route payload (including the slow details) on link hover/viewport intersection. ## What the goal requires Two separate things: 1. **Title appears instantly** — split the title into its own `` boundary with its own fast data fetch, so it resolves and streams in before the 800ms details. The current `getProjectTitle` is already fast (no delay), so it just needs its own boundary rather than being co-awaited with the slow one. 2. **Don't prefetch the rest of the project page** — disable prefetching on the dashboard ``s so navigating to a project doesn't eagerly fetch the heavy details payload ahead of time. Let me make both changes.

events.content:
Build passes cleanly. The route is now marked ◐ (Partial Prerender) — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content, which is exactly the streaming behavior we want.

## Summary

Two changes, addressing the two distinct requirements:

1. Title appears instantly — app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx

Split the single <Project> component (which co-awaited the fast title and the 800ms details via Promise.all) into two independent async components, each in its own <Suspense> boundary:
- <ProjectTitle> — awaits only getProjectTitle (no delay), so the <h1> resolves and streams in immediately.
- <ProjectDetails> — awaits only getProjectDetails (the 800ms fetch), showing Loading details... until it's ready.

Because they're separate Suspense boundaries, the slow details no longer block the title from streaming. The build confirms this via the ◐ (Partial Prerender) marker, meaning the shell + title prerender statically and the details stream in.

2. Don't prefetch the rest of the project page — app/page.tsx

Added prefetch={false} to the dashboard <Link>s. With cacheComponents: true, Next.js would otherwise eagerly prefetch the full route payload (including the heavy details) on hover/viewport. prefetch={false} makes navigation fetch only on click.

Verification: npm run build exited 0, compiled successfully, TypeScript passed, and the project route is now a Partial Prerender.
